method.method_draft: Use coordinates and the diagonal-area formula. From the image, take the equilateral triangles to be constructed outward from the square, with K above AB, L to the right of BC, M below CD, and N to the left of DA. From the text, the square has area 16, so its side length is 4. Place the square centered at the origin with A=(-2,2), B=(2,2), C=(2,-2), D=(-2,-2). The altitude of each equilateral triangle of side 4 is 2√3, so K=(0,2+2√3), L=(2+2√3,0), M=(0,-2-2√3), and N=(-2-2√3,0). Thus diagonals KM and LN of KLMN are perpendicular and each has length 4+4√3. Compute area(KLMN)=1/2(4+4√3)^2=32+16√3.

claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: The lengths of diagonals KM and LN are both 4+4√3.

claims.claim: The area of a quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular to each other equals half the product of the lengths of the two diagonals.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: They are perpendicular to each other, and both have length 4+4√3. Thus the area is 1/2(4+4√3)^2
